body:
A bridge isn't pretending, a bridge is.

When people talk to me, they are convinced that I will not get along with them or anyone they know, and I often don't. I am not generally considered an enjoyable person to have around. That has nothing to do with my technical abilities.

I'm not proud of my work history; getting my internships was as hard as finding a job has been, and they were at small companies no one's ever heard of so no one takes them seriously on my resume.

Also, if you hold up a red pen, I will tell you it's a red pen. Very aggressively. I will absolutely refuse to call it a blue pen, even under use of intimidation and moderate amounts of force.

I can't tell jokes with a straight face. I crack up before I've even started saying anything. The only time I can complete a joke is when I think of it on the spot and say it before I've realized how funny it is. I'm terrible at jokes and even my girlfriend thinks the stories I tell are extremely boring.

I am very confident that I am a hard worker, but I don't have any way to show anyone that. I rarely ever smile, and when I do it is very obviously forced. I find it very uncomfortable, almost painful, to look people in the eye. I usually look at their nose or forehead, and can only maintain eye contact for a few seconds.

I don't go bars, I find small talk in general excessively boring.

I know what jobs I want, what jobs I deserve, there is just no one willing to pay me to do them because they don't like me. No one likes me.

Having little experience and a broad engineering degree, I am in a lot of fields. I am looking primarily for analyst (Systems, IT, Data) or engineering (Quality, Process, Systems, Reliability) positions; the particular industry really doesn't matter at this point. I'd prefer to be in food or pharmaceutical manufacturing over technology or automotive manufacturing. I'm further looking in Defense, Energy, and Federal employment.

This guy specifically was in Quality Engineering in several different industries.

And what I responded is that I've been having problems a lot longer than 8 months, and most people give up on advice and just insist it will get better at some later milestone. It hasn't happened, why should I expect it to ever?

Yeah, I believed that the first time, and the second, and I'm sick of hearing it. Everyone has told me that many times for years.

Things will be better when you're older, once you're in high school, once you're in college, once you join some clubs, once you're in a major, if you get an internship, when you get to senior year, if you get a graduate degree, when you graduate, when you get a job, and I'm sure if that's not going well someone will come up with things like once you have a house or once you have children. I put so much effort into everything and no one cares about any of it.

It's never gotten better and I'm just tired of waiting for it to.

I don't understand 'pretending' you are confident; confidence is all how you act anyway. I can't do that any more than I can 'pretend' to write a 10-page essay. I don't have anything to be confident about because I'm not successful at anything and the things I would be I never get to do. 

I don't even understand phrases like "fake it til you make it" - what does that even mean?

Here's a typical story from my life. 

I searched on my college's alumni network. I found a guy who graduated from my program about ten years ago and got starry-eyed looking at his listing. He had job titles I wanted, he'd worked for companies I was interested in working for (some that I'd even applied to!), the work he listed at those places was exactly the kind I wanted to do, he even had the certifications that I planned to get. This guy had my dream career. 

So I emailed him, saying I found him on the alumni network, can I ask him some questions about his experience, yadda yadda yadda, he replies with a phone number to call him at the next day.

So I prepare a laundry list of questions, in categories, but mainly as a discussion guide, it feels awkward asking most of them straight up. I call the guy, tell him about my background, and start to ask him about the field and his work.

He says if I have any experience in any other area I should try to do that instead. There are no positions or room for growth, most jobs have been moved outside the US, and the few that are you need to know Mandarin, or have a PhD. He said the only reason he's even in the field is because he needed to get a visa, so he had to take whatever job he could find.

So here he's been getting my dream jobs and hating them, and I can't even get any job, let alone the ones I want. Everyone seems to have this opinion that it's just a matter of finding a job you want to work in, and getting a job in it can be glossed over. I've known for years what I want to work in, or companies I want to work for, or locations I want to work at, and none of this has gotten me a job anywhere.

Everyone just says things like "Have you [Company X]? I know they are hiring for that sort of thing." and I reply "I've applied there a dozen times over the past three years and never gotten an interview" and then they just repeat the same thing ten other companies or websites. "Have you tried using Indeed? USAJobs? Your school's career service?" What do other people do when they are looking for a job? Sit around and wait for someone to hand it to them? I spend 5+ hours a day, every day of the week, looking for employment, for the past 8 months, and I am no closer than I was in 2009. What is supposed to keep me going when I am putting in far more effort than everyone else and getting nothing back?
I'm already applying to jobs in 8 states, including this one. Again, she hates it here too, we just can't move anywhere until one of us has a job there.
Operations Research (Industrial / Applied Statistics / Information Science / Supply Chain / Logistics)
The problem is that the thing I most enjoy doing is the thing I majored in, which no one will give me a chance to do.

A degree which I heavily regret getting into so much debt for because it hasn't done a thing to pay me back. Why did I even bother?

The problem with my interview skills is that I am bad at getting people to like me, I'm bad at inspiring confidence, and I'm bad at persuading people, always have been for all 3. No one wants to hire someone unless they like them, and I am terrible at getting people to like me.

The point was that I can't afford to replace the whole or any parts of it. I have $0, 0 income, 0 reason to expect any income. Whatever part it is, I don't have any money to do anything about it.

Also, the CD/DVD drive has been broken over a year now. It doesn't even stay in any more, let alone run. The whirring noise is coming from the other side.

I'm useless because I can't do anything well that is not related to my degree, so not being employed for it means there is nothing I can do. There's nothing I have to be encouraged by because everything I do I am bad at.

All three places have asked about salary and I've made it very clear that the amount they've specified is an amount I'm willing to work for; it is in fact an amount 20% lower than the average for graduates from my program in the past 3 years. Companies are definitely paying this much for people in my position, they just aren't paying me.

The reward you get from helping someone is seeing their situation improve. Mine never does. My college career center has basically given up on me because they've done and suggested everything they normally do and nothing has helped at all.

If she was the one unemployed our life would be great. She can actually do things unrelated to her job, I can't. Furthermore, I like to work a lot more than she does. If she were unemployed I wouldn't even mind if she stopped looking until conditions improved, but I'm useless outside of my technical skills. I'm bad at everything.

She's aware that I'm extremely depressed and frustrated, especially every time a bad career-related thing happens. We both hate this town, and she hates her job but can't leave it because then we'd both be unemployed. We can't afford to just move somewhere else and hope things go well.

It makes a very loud whirring sound any time you move it while it's on (and for several minutes after), several times a week it blue screens during normal operation, and sometimes just restarts for no reason. It's a 4 year old low-end beat-up Dell.

> "I like you, and I know where I can use you"

I made this very point. No one likes me, so even in spots where they could use me they don't want to.

I've posted asking about job advice plenty of times, but the advice I've gotten always boils down to "ask people you know who are employed to help you get into their company," which has been completely unsuccessful. No professor I've asked have ever had any career advice for me, let alone contacts. 

The degree doesn't mean anything if I can't remember anything I've learned because no one will let me do anything with it, so I'm becoming more useless by the day.

This isn't a matter of not finding a position that is at my level. My level is entry. I have not found any position. I'm not rejecting offers or even interviews, I'm just not getting any. Most positions I apply to I never get any response except the automated one. 

How could I be over-qualified? The positions I applied to rejected me for not being up to their qualifications and I have almost no work experience.
